summary: Regency dandy George 'Beau' Brummell rose from Eton and the Prince of Wales's own regiment to dictate London men's fashion around 1800, shaping the modern suit and celebrity culture, before debt and a feud with the prince drove him into exile in France.

evidence.note: birth in 1778 at Downing Street, father secretary to Lord North
long segment on Eton culture begins: classics, uniforms, drinking
Eton flogging rituals and prefect beatings of young boys described
fagging system and sexual abuse of younger pupils discussed
teen first love made pregnant by a married colonel, shunned by society
extended segment on the Prince of Wales and his show regiment
joins the 10th Light Dragoons at sixteen, wins the prince's favour
serves as best man at the prince's disastrous royal wedding
lives on credit, gambling debts mount once royal protection ends
final years in France: syphilis, imagined balls, dies in an asylum at 62

notes: Roles: no role fits a fashion icon or socialite; entertainer-artist is the closest, influencer-online rejected because he predates the internet. The hosts conclude he was not really a bastard but it is not billed as a hero episode, so deep-dive.
